ED Clerking - 11/03/2020, 13:46

Presenting complaint: Five-day history of fever, dry cough and increasing breathlessness in a woman in her 60s-70s.

History: Worsening dyspnoea on exertion, subjective fevers and non-productive cough. No chest pain. No known COVID-19 contact reported. Background of hypertension. Independent at baseline, lives with family.

Observations: Temperature 38.1°C, HR 104 bpm, BP 132/78 mmHg, SpO2 89% on air recorded at 06:52 on 11/03/2020, subsequently improved to 94% on 2L nasal cannula. NEWS2 score 6.

Examination: Tachypnoeic at rest, bilateral fine crackles at both lung bases, no wheeze. Cardiovascular and abdominal examination unremarkable. Alert and orientated.

Swab taken for SARS-CoV-2 PCR given clinical suspicion of COVID-19; sample sent to virology.

Impression: Suspected COVID-19 pneumonia with hypoxiaemia.

Plan: Admit under medicine for oxygen therapy, monitoring and further investigation including chest X-ray and bloods (FBC, U&E, CRP, D-dimer). VTE risk assessment completed - high risk, enoxaparin thromboprophylaxis to be prescribed once weight and renal function confirmed. Patient initially declined admission and wished to go home; agreed to stay after discussion with family. Admitted to hospital at 12:21 on 11/03/2020. Isolation precautions in side room as per COVID-19 pathway. Repeat observations 4-hourly, escalate if deteriorating.

ED Clerking
